basis: Hydroxylysine metabolism disorder defined by seizures and intellectual disability; aminoaciduria alone does not establish renal damage.
Dens invaginatus is a structural developmental disorder of teeth; teeth and palate fall within the gastrointestinal axis.
Phosphoglucomutase enzyme entry suggests carbohydrate metabolism; supplied record establishes no clinical phenotype or specific organ damage.
Intestinal fluke infection; ectopic organ infection is occasional and does not qualify.
Rickettsial infection; acute cutaneous signs do not establish common lasting organ dysfunction.
Glyoxylate metabolism disorder defined by renal oxalate deposition, nephrocalcinosis and recurrent stones; no common extra-renal damage established.
Skeletal myopathy with muscle atrophy; respiratory insufficiency (9/14) and dysphagia (10/14) reflect muscle weakness rather than direct lung or gut damage.
CRYBB1-related isolated early-onset cataract; manifestations are confined to the eyes.
Primary antibody immunodeficiency; infections and organ complications vary across subtypes and do not establish common direct extra-immune damage.
Inherited epidermal fragility with blistering and erosions; muscle, kidney and hearing involvement belongs to uncommon subtypes.
Benign tumor arising in the subglottic airway; no additional organ damage established.
Skeletal dysplasia, cataracts and developmental delay define the syndrome; cleft palate is a defining feature despite its 5-29% HPO annotation.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; joint hypermobility and pes planus occur in 80-99%, scoliosis in 30-79%. Otitis, sinusitis and reflux are separate diseases.
Intrinsic immune dysregulation causes autoimmune hemolysis/thrombocytopenia in 2/3; bronchiectasis/chronic lung disease (2/3) follows separate infections.
Focal epilepsy with preserved awareness is a disorder of cerebral electrical function.
Inherited lipid metabolism disorder with neuropathy and hearing loss; ocular damage includes cataracts in 15/19 and rod-cone dystrophy in 7/19.
Atrial cardiac rhythm disorder; stroke and other embolic events are separate complications.
Primary middle-ear tumor causing conductive hearing loss; neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish an endocrine gland disorder.
Pharyngeal disease umbrella; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis. Infectious and neoplastic subtypes do not define the entire group.
Manifesting dystrophinopathy defined by progressive skeletal myopathy; cardiomyopathy and ventricular hypertrophy are occasional (5-29%).
Retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy causing progressive visual loss; associated abnormalities remain ocular.
Inherited keratinization disorder producing skin blistering followed by hyperkeratosis.
Inherited melanin synthesis disorder defined by skin/hair hypopigmentation and impaired ocular pigmentation, development and visual acuity.
Psychotic disorder falls outside the axes; cognitive symptoms and unspecified EEG abnormalities do not establish a separate neurologic organ disease.
Rickettsial spotted-fever infection; no evidence establishes common lasting damage to an additional organ.
